::: notes
Welcome. Two halves, one break, and one published claim throughout: a study of what the European Union means to the people of its member states, and of whether the economic crisis changed that. In the first half I give you the vocabulary of three kinds of repetition, show you Multi100 from the inside, as one of the five analysts who reanalysed this claim, then the paper itself and what SCORE found when it checked it. You write down the question that the claim answers, and before the break you reproduce the result that one of the analysts recorded. In the second half you become the sixth analyst: you take the analysis apart into its decisions, try alternatives in the browser lab, put the one that you would defend on the class chart, and we read the class against every justifiable analysis of these data. Nothing needs installing.
:::

## What you do not need {#what-you-do-not-need}

::: {.none}
- No installation: the browser lab runs R inside a tab of your browser, with the data in place
- No git, and no GitHub account
- No OSF account – we read the OSF as readers, without logging in
- Nothing leaves your machine except the one result that you choose to send to the class chart
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Do this now:** open the browser lab in a tab and leave it to load. R loads in the page while we talk; once it has, run the three cells of Task 1.
:::
